papers.abstract_en: Oesophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma (OGJ AC) represents an increasingly prevalent malignancy for which treatment recommendations remain challenging, as patients are frequently included within trials addressing gastric or oesophageal cancer. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) published between 2000 and 2025 including patients with OGJ AC to provide a comprehensive assessment of contemporary treatment strategies for this disease across all stages. A total of 100 high-quality RCTs including more than 13,000 patients with OGJ tumours were identified. In localized disease, 36 studies evaluated surgical procedures, adjuvant/neoadjuvant/perioperative treatments and definitive approaches. Surgery is still the cornerstone of curative treatment, increasingly incorporating minimally invasive techniques. Perioperative chemotherapy and chemoimmunotherapy represent standard approaches, while neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy followed by adjuvant nivolumab represents an alternative strategy. In advanced disease, 64 studies assessed systemic therapies in first/second/third lines or palliative interventions. Platinum-fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy persists as the backbone of first-line treatment, with treatment intensification guided by biomarkers. While the benefit of trastuzumab in HER2-positive tumours appears greater in OGJ than in gastric cancer, the opposite pattern is observed with zolbetuximab in CLDN18.2-positive tumours. Several trials testing anti-PD-1 therapies confirm their activity in OGJ AC, despite the predictive value of PD-L1 appearing uncertain in this anatomical subgroup. In later lines, paclitaxel plus ramucirumab, trastuzumab deruxtecan for HER2-positive disease, and trifluridine-tipiracil remain established options. The available evidence suggests clinically meaningful differences in treatment efficacy according to tumour location, supporting the consideration of OGJ AC as a distinct disease entity. Dedicated OGJ AC trials incorporating standardized anatomical classification are needed to improve outcomes in this aggressive disease.

papers.title_zh: CLDN18.2免疫组化鉴别肺浸润性黏液腺癌与非黏液NSCLC的诊断效能：敏感度89.3%、特异度97.6%
papers.title_en: Claudin 18.2 as a specific diagnostic marker for pulmonary invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma.
papers.authors: Byun J, Seo AN, Yoon G, Park JY, Kim M
papers.affiliation_highlight: Department of Pathology, Daegu Fatima Hospital, Daegu, Republic of Korea.
papers.results: CLDN18.2在75/84例IMA（89.3%）阳性，而在82例其他NSCLC中仅2例（2.4%）阳性；CLDN18.2的H-score在IMA显著高于其他NSCLC（均值±SD，216.6±105.3 vs. 1.6±13.8；P<0.001）。CLDN18.2诊断效能：敏感度89.3%（95% CI, 80.9-94.3），特异度97.6%（95% CI, 91.5-99.3），阳性预测值97.4%（95% CI, 91.0-99.3），阴性预测值89.9%（95% CI, 81.9-94.6）。HNF4A与MUC5AC敏感度略高，但特异度低于CLDN18.2（摘要未给出具体数值）。
papers.authors_conclusion: CLDN18.2是肺IMA的一种高特异性免疫组化标志物，与HNF4A和MUC5AC相比具有更优的确诊（rule-in）效能。
papers.ai_note: 阳性阈值设为H-score>0（任何着色即阳性）极为宽松，阈值未做ROC优化或敏感性分析；84:82的病例构成近似病例-对照抽样，PPV/NPV不能外推至真实患病率人群；仅纳入手术切除标本，缺少活检/细胞学小标本验证，存在谱偏倚（spectrum bias）；单中心、无外部验证队列；摘要称HNF4A/MUC5AC特异度更低但未报告其具体数值，无法核实'更优rule-in'的量化依据；未报告阅片者间一致性。信息不足：CLDN18.2在黏液型与非黏液型腺癌之外其他胃型分化肿瘤中的交叉表达情况未描述。

pico.p: 手术切除的肺肿瘤患者，包括84例浸润性黏液腺癌（IMA）和82例其他非小细胞肺癌（NSCLC）

papers.reason: 为病理诊断中肺浸润性黏液腺癌的免疫组化鉴别提供标志物选择依据（CLDN18.2 vs HNF4A/MUC5AC），影响黏液性肺腺癌的病理分型与后续治疗决策参考；其诊断效能数据可作为后续验证研究的对照基线。
papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2) is physiologically expressed in normal gastric epithelium and is frequently retained in gastric adenocarcinoma. Recent studies have suggested that CLDN18.2 may also be expressed in tumors showing gastric epitheliallike differentiation outside the stomach, including pulmonary invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma (IMA). This study evaluated the diagnostic utility of CLDN18.2 compared with HNF4A and MUC5AC in pulmonary IMA. METHODS: We assessed immunohistochemical expression of CLDN18.2 using clone 43-14A, HNF4A, and MUC5AC in surgically resected pulmonary tumors, including 84 IMAs and 82 other non-small cell lung carcinomas (NSCLCs). Staining was semiquantitatively evaluated using H-scores, and positivity was defined as an H-score greater than 0. Diagnostic performance was assessed using sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV), with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). RESULTS: CLDN18.2 was positive in 75 of 84 IMAs (89.3%) but in only 2 of 82 other NSCLCs (2.4%). CLDN18.2H-scores were markedly higher in IMA than in other NSCLC (mean ± SD, 216.6 ± 105.3 vs. 1.6 ± 13.8; P < 0.001). CLDN18.2 showed a sensitivity of 89.3% (95% CI, 80.9-94.3), specificity of 97.6% (95% CI, 91.5-99.3), PPV of 97.4% (95% CI, 91.0-99.3), and NPV of 89.9% (95% CI, 81.9-94.6). Although HNF4A and MUC5AC showed slightly higher sensitivities, their specificities were lower than that of CLDN18.2. CONCLUSIONS: CLDN18.2 is a highly specific immunohistochemical marker for pulmonary IMA and provides superior rule-in performance compared with HNF4A and MUC5AC.

papers.abstract_en: Metabolic plasticity enables tumors to adapt to fluctuating nutrient environments, yet the non-canonical functions of metabolic enzymes under stress remain largely unexplored. Here, we established a pyrimidine biosynthesis-associated gene score (PBAGS) that predicts survival in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and identified dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHODH) as a critical driver with a context-dependent dual role. Under glucose-replete conditions, DHODH functions as a canonical oncogene, promoting pyrimidine and cysteine metabolism, alongside UDP-GlcNAc production; accordingly, its inhibition by leflunomide suppresses tumor growth. Strikingly, under glucose starvation, DHODH undergoes a functional switch to become a "molecular executioner." Mechanistically, starvation triggers the DHODH-OGT axis to maintain site-specific O-GlcNAcylation of SLC7A11 at Ser26, thereby stabilizing SLC7A11. This modification promotes excessive cystine accumulation and subsequent actin cytoskeleton collapse, ultimately triggering disulfidptosis. Accordingly, inhibition of DHODH abolishes this modification and rescues cells from starvation-induced death. Clinically, DHODH-SLC7A11 axis correlates tightly with GLUT1 expression. Mimicking glucose starvation using GLUT1 inhibitor BAY-876 significantly enhances radiosensitivity in ESCC PDX models that harbor high DHODH/SLC7A11 expression. Collectively, our findings uncover that under glucose starvation, DHODH and SLC7A11 co-dependency synergistically promotes disulfidptosis, suggesting that targeting the metabolic context offers a potent strategy to sensitize ESCC to radiotherapy.

papers.title_en: RESPONSE-ADAPTIVE STEREOTACTIC BODY RADIOTHERAPY BOOST AFTER CONCURRENT CHEMORADIOTHERAPY IN UNRESECTABLE STAGE III NSCLC: A PROSPECTIVE SINGLE-CENTRE COHORT STUDY.
papers.authors: Kiraz E, Eroğlu C, Gündoğ M, Bozkurt O, Karabıyık Ö, Abdülrezzak Ü, Aksözen MT
papers.affiliation_highlight: Erciyes University, Faculty of Medicine, Department of Radiation Oncology, Kayseri, Turkey.
papers.results: 中位随访26个月；2年OS 61.5%、2年LRC 62.8%；中位PFS 13个月、中位DMFS 16个月；远处转移为主要失败模式，占41.2%；残余原发累积剂量<94.77 Gy(EQD2)独立预测更差LRC（HR 5.86）；3个月残余原发SUVmax≥4.55预测更差LRC（HR 5.04）；OS独立相关因素为残余淋巴结体积、3个月代谢进展及后续局区进展；3-4级放射性肺炎7.8%，3级食管炎1例（2%），咯血5例（9.8%）

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to escalate the dose to the residual primary tumor with an adaptive stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) boost after concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in unresectable stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), and to explore, within this cohort, whether a higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control (LRC) and whether this translated into a difference in overall survival (OS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this single-center, prospective, single-arm cohort, 51 patients received concurrent CRT (50 Gy/25 fractions with weekly carboplatin and paclitaxel) followed by an adaptive boost (30 Gy/5 fractions to the residual primary, 10 Gy/5 fractions to residual nodes), without consolidation durvalumab. Doses were summed by deformable registration and reported as EQD2. Response was assessed at 3 months with FDG-PET/CT (PERCIST), and toxicity with CTCAE v5.0. Outcomes estimated by Kaplan-Meier; predictors by Cox regression. RESULTS: At a median follow-up of 26 months, 2-year OS and LRC were 61.5% and 62.8%. The median PFS and DMFS were 13 and 16 months, and distant metastasis was the dominant failure pattern (41.2%). Cumulative dose below 94.77 Gy (EQD2) to the residual primary independently predicted worse LRC (HR 5.86), and a 3-month locoregional SUVmax ≥4.55 predicted worse LRC (HR 5.04). OS was independently associated with residual nodal volume, 3-month metabolic progression, and subsequent locoregional progression. Grade 3-4 pneumonitis occurred in 7.8%, grade 3 esophagitis in one patient (2%), and hemoptysis in five (9.8%). CONCLUSION: The SBRT boost achieved encouraging locoregional control, including in bulky and node-advanced disease, without immunotherapy, and higher cumulative dose to the residual primary was associated with better locoregional control. Hemoptysis was the main safety concern and occurred predominantly in patients with pre-existing hemoptysis, supporting careful selection and strict bronchial constraints. Local escalation alone did not overcome the competing risk of distant failure.

papers.abstract_en: INTRODUCTION: The interplay between donor type, machine perfusion, and donor organ out of body (OOB) time on post-lung transplant outcomes remains poorly understood. METHODS: We analyzed outcomes of 28,120 adult lung transplant recipients from the UNOS database (2012-2024) to evaluate the impact of OOB time by donor type (donation after brain death, DBD vs circulatory death, DCD) and use of machine perfusion on one-year post-lung transplant mortality. Fifty-four donor, recipient, and procedural variables were included in a Light Gradient Boosting Machine model, with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) used to quantify predictor effects. RESULTS: Recipient age, renal function, and OOB time were the strongest predictors of one-year post-transplant mortality. A logarithmic relationship was observed between OOB time and mortality, with a distinct threshold at 400 minutes beyond which predicted mortality increased sharply (p<0.01). Below this threshold, SHAP values were negative across donor types and perfusion status, indicating favorable contributions to survival. Beyond 400 minutes, SHAP values shifted positive, with DCD organs demonstrating the highest vulnerability. Mortality risk in DCD recipients exceeded that of DBD recipients at any OOB time, while machine-perfused grafts showed greater variability in risk. CONCLUSIONS: These findings identify OOB time > 400 minutes as a critical determinant of post-transplant mortality with substantially amplified risk among DCD allografts.

papers.abstract_en: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the independent and combined prognostic impact of weight loss, disease severity, and forced vital capacity (FVC) decline in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) using time-updated and landmark analyses. METHODS: We retrospectively analysed 2697 visits from 667 patients with IPF followed at a single tertiary centre. Annualised changes in body weight and FVC were calculated at each visit. Time updated flexible parametric survival models were used to assess associations with transplant-free survival, adjusting for disease severity (Composite Physiologic Index, CPI) and clinical covariates. Landmark analyses at 1-4 years and joint longitudinal survival models were also performed. RESULTS: In time-updated analyses, higher CPI (HR (95% CI): 2.75 (2.28-3.33)) per 10-point increase, ≥5% annual weight loss (HR: 1.85 (1.31-2.52)), and ≥10 percentage point annual decline in FVC% predicted (HR: 2.26 (1.66-3.10)) were independently associated with transplant-free survival. Patients meeting both thresholds for weight loss and FVC decline had a markedly increased risk (HR: 4.11 (2.65-6.40)), with no evidence of interaction. These findings were consistent across landmark analyses. Joint modelling confirmed their independent effect and showed that threshold-based changes were more strongly associated with transplant-free survival than continuous longitudinal trajectories. Reverse-time analysis suggested that the decline in both weight and FVC accelerates in the last months before death or transplant. CONCLUSIONS: Weight loss and FVC decline provide independent and additive prognostic information in IPF, with comparable effect sizes and consistency of the effect over time. Routine weight monitoring may improve risk stratification and help identify patients at high risk of adverse outcomes.

papers.abstract_en: Immune checkpoint inhibitors have improved outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet durable benefit remains uneven because tumor immunity is organized by cytokine and chemokine circuits that vary across anatomic niches and treatment states. This narrative review integrates single-cell, spatial, mechanistic and clinically annotated evidence around source-ligand-receptor-target relationships to assess how cytokine and chemokine circuits relate to ICI response and resistance in NSCLC, and what these findings imply for spatial biomarkers and combination strategies. Representative activating circuits reviewed here include XCL1/2-XCR1- and CCL5-dependent cDC1 recruitment, IL-12/IL-18-supported NK-cell activation, CXCL9/10-CXCR3-guided effector trafficking and CXCL13-CXCR5-dependent tertiary lymphoid structure organization. These programs may support antitumor immunity relevant to ICI response, whereas suppressive programs involving TGF-β, IL-10, CSF1, CCL2, IL-17, together with interacting pathways such as adenosine-mediated metabolic suppression, may contribute to immune exclusion and resistance in NSCLC. Clinical translation remains uneven: spatial biomarkers and pathway-directed combinations are supported mainly by cross-sectional cohorts, mechanistic studies and early clinical trials, with several negative or context-specific results. We therefore synthesize these findings and outline a conceptual, evidence-tiered framework that considers cellular source, receptor-bearing target, spatial niche, treatment history and pharmacodynamic evidence. By linking spatial immune organization to mechanisms of response and resistance, this framework provides a foundation for biomarker-informed combinations tailored to distinct immune dysfunctions, with the potential to overcome resistance and extend durable immunotherapy benefit to more patients with NSCLC.

papers.abstract_en: AIM: This pilot study evaluated the feasibility, acceptability and fidelity of digital video preoperative physiotherapy education compared with face-to-face education for patients undergoing thoracic surgery. It also explored clinical outcomes to inform a future non-inferiority trial of digital education. METHOD: This prospective pilot feasibility randomised controlled trial was conducted at a tertiary centre in Brisbane, Australia. Participants were randomly allocated to receive face-to-face physiotherapy education or watch a 13-minute professionally made digital education video before thoracic surgery. Protocol feasibility was assessed as the percentage of patients receiving allocated education. Acceptability was measured using a pre/postoperative questionnaire and postoperative interviews. Protocol fidelity, defined as recall of receiving education, and treatment fidelity, defined as recall of key information, were assessed during postoperative interviews using a preset 24-point scoring schema. Feasibility measures included recruitment, retention and missing data. Exploratory outcomes included postoperative pulmonary complications, hospital length of stay and efficiency. RESULTS: Sixty-four participants were randomised to face-to-face or digital education before thoracic surgery. All received allocated education, demonstrating 100% protocol feasibility. Both education modes were acceptable and perceived to help with information recall (87% vs 81%) and surgical recovery (93% vs 84%), and included the right amount of information (97% vs 84%). Protocol fidelity (83% vs 87%) and treatment fidelity (median 9.5 [interquartile range (IQR) 6-12] vs 9 [IQR 6-15]) were comparable between groups. Study feasibility was confirmed by 100% recruitment and retention and 95% complete datasets. Hospital length of stay and postoperative pulmonary complications were similar. Digital education was more efficient, saving a median of 10 minutes of preoperative physiotherapist time per patient. CONCLUSIONS: Digital preoperative physiotherapy education for patients undergoing thoracic surgery is feasible, acceptable and efficient, with protocol and treatment fidelity similar to face-to-face education.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Neuropsychiatric adverse effects (AEs) have increasingly been reported with elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor (ETI) in people with cystic fibrosis (PwCF). Vanzacaftor/tezacaftor/deutivacaftor (VTD) demonstrated similar rates of neuropsychiatric events to ETI in clinical trials; however, individuals with prior ETI intolerance were not specifically studied. We evaluated neuropsychiatric outcomes after switching from ETI to VTD in PwCF with documented ETI-related neuropsychiatric AEs. METHODS: We performed a retrospective chart review of adults with cystic fibrosis with documented ETI-related neuropsychiatric AEs who transitioned to VTD and had at least one follow-up visit. Patient-reported symptom changes, Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) scores were assessed before and after VTD initiation. Changes in screening scores were analyzed using Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Agreement between patient-reported improvement and clinically meaningful reductions in GAD-7 and PHQ-9 scores was evaluated using Cohen's kappa. RESULTS: Twenty-three patients were included (median age 40 years, 60.9% female). Nineteen (82.6%) reported improvement in neuropsychiatric symptoms after transitioning to VTD. GAD-7 scores improved significantly (median 6 [IQR: 2 -10] vs. 3 [IQR: 0-7], p=0.005), while PHQ-9 scores decreased from a median of 6 [IQR: 2-9] to 3 [IQR: 2-8], p=0.05. Agreement between patient-reported improvement and clinically meaningful changes in GAD-7 (κ = -0.107, 95% CI [-0.351, 0.136], p=0.81) and PHQ-9 (κ = 0.123, 95% CI [0.077, 0.323], p=0.12), was poor to slight. CONCLUSIONS: Most PwCF with ETI-related neuropsychiatric AEs reported improvement after switching to VTD. Standard anxiety and depression screening tools may not fully capture CFTR modulator-associated neuropsychiatric symptoms. Larger prospective studies are needed.

papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Tuberculosis (TB) treatment remains hindered by three intertwined challenges, drug delivery barriers, immune evasion, and high relapse rates. Despite advances in nanocarriers and immunomodulation, an integrated platform that achieves precise targeting, potent sterilisation, immune remodelling, and durable protection is still lacking. METHODS: A biomimetic DNA tetrahedral phototherapy system (TDN + AIE@MM) was constructed using Mycobacterium marinum membrane modification to mimic trained immunity and enable dual spatiotemporal targeting of granulomas and lymph nodes. Through natural membrane ligand recognition, the system delivered payloads to immunosuppressive granulomas and antigen-retarded lymph nodes. Upon NIR-II irradiation, the AIE agent generated local hyperthermia to kill intracellular Mycobacterium tuberculosis and released antigens to activate adaptive and long-term memory immune responses. FINDINGS: TDN + AIE@MM exhibited uniform size, good stability, and preserved membrane proteins. In vitro, it showed superior targeting to H37Ra and macrophages over unmodified controls. Under 808 nm laser irradiation, it achieved >99% killing of extra- and intracellular H37Ra, induced M1 polarisation with pro-inflammatory cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α), and enhanced T-cell proliferation and antigen-specific responses. In vivo, it achieved spatiotemporal dual-targeting to granulomas and lymph nodes, increased CD80+/CD86+ antigen-presenting cells and CD4+ T-cell activation, and reduced lung bacterial load. For immune memory, TRM (CD8+CD69+CD103+) reached 21.8% on day 42, approximately two-fold higher than rifampicin (Rif). In a rechallenge relapse model, the 84-day relapse rate was 16.7% versus 66.7% for Rif, with higher memory B cells and TEM, confirming durable protection. INTERPRETATION: These findings show that TDN + AIE@MM integrates physical sterilisation, immunosuppression reversal, and durable immune memory via dual spatiotemporal targeting, effectively addressing the three core challenges in TB therapy, namely delivery barriers, immune evasion, and relapse risk, and offering a promising strategy for immunotherapy and relapse prevention. papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: Living near major roads may increase the short-term effects of ambient PM2.5 exposure on asthma exacerbations. We evaluated whether residential proximity to major roads modifies the association between ambient PM2.5 and asthma emergency department (ED) visits in Lima, Peru. METHODS: We analyzed asthma ED visits from 10 public hospitals in Lima (2017-2023) using a time-stratified case-crossover design. We used a high-resolution (1×1 km) multi-source model to assign daily mean PM2.5, temperature, and relative humidity to geocoded residences. We classified residential proximity to major roadways (>75th percentile of traffic volume) by distance thresholds from 100 to 500 m. Using conditional logistic regression with distributed lag non-linear models, we estimated lag-specific and cumulative associations and tested for effect modification. RESULTS: We included 75,602 asthma ED visits (mean age 16.2 years; 50.7% male) matched to 258,120 control-days. PM2.5 was associated with higher odds of ED visits across lags 0-15 days, with the strongest lag-specific association at lag 0. The exposure-response relationship was steeper at lower PM2.5 concentrations. At lag 0, an increase in PM2.5 from 5 to 15 μg/m3 was associated with 9% higher odds of an ED visit (OR=1.09, 95% CI 1.01-1.16). Cumulative associations over lags 0-15 days were higher among residents living within 400 m of a major roadway (OR=4.02, 95% CI 1.97-8.19) than among those living at ≥400 m (OR=1.66, 95% CI 0.81-3.38; interaction p-value=0.04). CONCLUSIONS: Short-term increases in ambient PM2.5 were associated with higher odds of asthma ED visits, with a steeper exposure-response relationship at lower concentrations and effects accumulating over the preceding 15 days. Associations were consistently stronger among residents living within pre-specified proximity thresholds to major roadways, supporting a pattern compatible with effect modification.

papers.abstract_en: Seasonal influenza vaccines require annual reformulation due to antigenic drift and provide suboptimal protection. Here, we evaluate self-amplifying mRNA (samRNA) vaccines encoding chimeric (cHA) and mosaic (mHA) hemagglutinins representing influenza A virus HA phylogenetic groups 1 and 2. Following prime-boost immunization, group 1 cHA vaccines (cH8/1-cH5/1) elicit broad cross-reactive antibodies and confer complete protection against diverse H1N1 strains covering decades of antigenic drift. Group 2 vaccines (cH4/3-cH15/3 and mH10/3-mH14/3) provide comparable breadth against multiple H3N2 strains and heterosubtypic H7N9 challenge, with cHA samRNA showing superior cross-group protection. Protection is associated with Fc-mediated effector functions and CD4+ T cell responses, with minimal hemagglutination inhibition and neutralizing titers. Passive serum transfer confirms antibody-mediated protection independent of cellular immunity. Protective immunity is maintained at doses as low as 0.4 μg, demonstrating the dose-sparing advantage of the samRNA platform. These results support samRNA-delivered cHA and mHA antigens as promising candidates for broadly protective influenza vaccines.

papers.abstract_en: Aging in cystic fibrosis (CF), once a hopeful possibility, is now a celebrated reality for many and attributable to expert multidisciplinary care, persistent research efforts, and fervent advocacy. The median age of survival of people with CF (PWCF) increased dramatically with the advent of cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator modulator therapies, particularly elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor in 2019. However, as PWCF live longer, healthy aging is susceptible to the compound impact of residual CFTR dysfunction, chronic inflammation, emerging comorbidities, complexities of chronic disease management, and psychosocial burdens. We define healthy aging as maintaining physical and mental health in adults so they can remain autonomous and independent as long as possible, while also adapting lifestyle habits to support well-being and improve overall quality of life. Lifestyle factors, such as stress, nutrition, physical activity, sleep, and treatment adherence, are known to impact health outcomes in the general population. Identifying, testing, and implementing behavioral interventions addressing these factors has the potential to augment medical advances in CF care. Although the aging population of PWCF is increasingly heterogeneous and shaped by unique individual ecosystems, lifestyle behaviors impact all patients and crosscut this diversity. As CF science continues to advance toward curative therapies, parallel CF-specific research advances on modifiable lifestyle behaviors may support healthier aging and improve health outcomes. This paper outlines the current state of knowledge, identifies critical gaps, and highlights key opportunities for future research targeting modifiable lifestyle behaviors to promote healthy aging, preserve functional independence, and improve quality of life in the growing population of adults with CF.
